# tcpdump

`tcpdump` &middot; _sniffing-spoofing_

Captures packet headers on an interface, or reads an existing capture.

**Moderate impact.** It touches the target directly; keep the scope tight.

## What this tool needs

- For live capture, an interface you are allowed to capture on and root.
- Because WSL2 sits behind a NAT it sees little of your real LAN; capture on Windows instead and analyse the file here.

## How to use it

Use a capture expression to limit traffic (e.g. `port 53`). Write to a file with `-w` and analyse it later. Only capture traffic you are authorised to see.

## Examples

```console
$ tcpdump -i eth0 -n port 53
$ tcpdump -i any -w capture.pcap -c 500
```
